children: Brazil's electoral authority TSE said on Sunday it had temporarily paused vote counting in the country's presidential runoff after a Supreme Court justice ruled that voting hours be extended nationwide by two hours.

Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva took an early lead before the count was paused, with 57.66% of valid votes compared with 42.34% for right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro after 0.25% of ballots had been counted, according to TSE.
The initial tally was too small to indicate a voting trend in the nationwide election.
